$comment: CYP-744 §3-ii parity oracle. GENERATED from the CYP-704 client resolver (web-ts mentionModel.ts) — do not hand-edit; regenerate with UPDATE_MENTION_FIXTURES=1. Offsets are UTF-16 code units over `body`, `end` is EXCLUSIVE. The server implementation of CYP-744 must reproduce `expected` exactly for every case.

cases.name: plain-mention
cases.why: a roster-known token is one mention; surrounding text stays intact

cases.name: unknown-token-fail-closed
cases.why: FALSE-POSITIVE GUARD: an unknown handle is NOT a mention — claiming someone was addressed when nobody is called that is the core lie

cases.name: email-not-a-mention
cases.why: a sigil mid-word is not a mention: in mail@dev5.de the preceding `l` is an id character

cases.name: empty-roster-resolves-nothing
cases.why: UNLOADED or FAILED roster ⇒ plain text, never a guessed mention (CYP-288 tie-in)

cases.name: multiple-mentions
cases.why: several mentions in one body; the connecting text stays text

cases.name: longest-match-wins
cases.why: with both `front` and `frontend` on the roster, `@frontend` resolves to the LONGER id

cases.name: boundary-terminated
cases.why: THE WRONG-PERSON GUARD: `@frontend-dev` must not highlight `frontend`, because `-` is itself a legal id character

cases.name: boundary-terminated-resolves-full-id
cases.why: the same body DOES resolve when the full id is on the roster

cases.name: punctuation-stops-at-id
cases.why: longest-match stops at the id; trailing punctuation stays text

cases.name: bracketed
cases.why: Tester2 F2: (@dev5) is an ordinary way to write a mention

cases.name: quoted-inline
cases.why: Tester2 F2: "@dev5" resolves while the email guard still holds

cases.name: case-insensitive-canonical-id
cases.why: people type @Frontend; the id reported is CANONICAL, the text stays verbatim

cases.name: underscore-id
cases.why: `_` is an id character, not a break

cases.name: fenced-code-exempt
cases.why: a handle in a snippet is being SHOWN, not addressed — must not summon anyone

cases.name: inline-code-exempt
cases.why: same rule for inline code

cases.name: unterminated-fence-exempt-to-end
cases.why: FAIL-CLOSED: an unterminated fence exempts to the end rather than half-parsing the body

cases.name: mention-after-closed-fence
cases.why: the exemption ENDS with the block — a later mention still resolves

cases.name: backtick-inside-fence-is-content
cases.why: a backtick inside a fence is content, not an inline delimiter

cases.name: code-exempt-beats-sigil-boundary
cases.why: the widened sigil boundary must not turn a backtick into a licence to mention

cases.name: quoted-line-still-mentions
cases.why: quoting someone who addressed you is STILL addressing — quotes are included, unlike code

cases.name: bare-sigil
cases.why: a bare `@` resolves to nothing and stays text

cases.name: blank-roster-id-ignored
cases.why: a blank/whitespace roster id must never swallow a bare sigil

cases.name: adjacent-mentions
cases.why: two mentions separated only by punctuation keep distinct spans

cases.name: mention-at-string-start
cases.why: position 0 is a valid sigil boundary

cases.name: utf16-offsets-after-astral-char
cases.why: OFFSET UNITS ARE UTF-16 CODE UNITS, end-EXCLUSIVE. An emoji outside the BMP counts as TWO units, so a server using code POINTS would report a span two short here. Without this case both conventions agree on every ASCII fixture and the disagreement ships silently.
